failures.title: Mitsubishi 4B11T Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch - Rattling & Performance Loss
items.whatHappens: The 4B11T uses a timing chain that can stretch over time, particularly on high‑mileage or heavily tuned examples. The tensioner is also prone to wear. Symptoms include rattling on cold start‑up, poor performance, and check‑engine lights. If the chain jumps, valves will contact pistons, resulting in catastrophic engine failure.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early (rattling only), timing chain and tensioner replacement is a manageable repair (£800-£1,500). If the chain has jumped, the engine is typically beyond economical repair - a full replacement is the only option. Read our full timing chain failure guide

items.title: Oil Consumption - Piston Ring Wear & PCV Issues
items.whatHappens: The 4B11T is known for oil consumption, particularly on high‑mileage examples. This can be due to worn piston rings, valve stem seals, or a faulty PCV valve. Excessive oil consumption can lead to low oil levels, which can cause bearing damage and turbo failure.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the PCV valve and using a heavier oil can reduce consumption. Piston ring replacement is a major job (£1,500-£3,000) and is often done as part of a rebuild. If the engine has suffered bearing damage due to low oil, a full replacement is required. Read our full oil consumption guide

items.title: Turbocharger Failure - Wastegate & Bearing Issues
items.whatHappens: The 4B11T's TD05HR turbocharger (and variants) can suffer from wastegate actuator failure, bearing wear, and oil seal failure. Symptoms include loss of boost, blue smoke, and a whining noise from the turbo. This is more common on tuned engines running higher boost.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbo refurbishment is a specialist job (£500-£1,200). If the turbo has failed catastrophically, it will send debris into the oil system, requiring a full engine strip and replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 4B11T was revised over its production life, with later engines (2012+) benefiting from improved piston rings and a revised timing chain tensioner. However, the core vulnerabilities remain - regular oil changes (5,000 miles) with high‑quality fully synthetic oil are essential. The engine is otherwise robust and capable of high mileage with proper maintenance.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 4B11T
variants.intro: The 4B11T is the turbocharged version of Mitsubishi's 2.0‑litre 4B11 engine, featuring a forged crankshaft, high‑strength connecting rods, and a cast aluminium block with closed‑deck design for strength. It is the engine of the Lancer Evolution X and was offered in multiple power outputs depending on the market and specification. Where the code appears: - Stamped on a metal plate on the engine block (left‑hand side, near the timing cover) - On the V5C logbook under "Engine number" (the first 5 characters will read 4B11T) - Via Mitsubishi VIN decoder - the Evo X is easily identifiable by chassis code CZ4A Commonly confused with: - 4B11 - the naturally aspirated 2.0‑litre petrol used in Lancer, Outlander and ASX; no turbocharger, different pistons and compression ratio - [4G63T - LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory] - the 2.0‑litre turbo from earlier Evos (I-IX); completely different engine family (iron block), not interchangeable - [4B11T - LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory] - different tunes (FQ‑335, FQ‑360, FQ‑400) are ECU and turbo variations, but the long‑block is similar

relatives.description: LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory] - the legendary 2.0‑litre turbocharged engine that powered the Lancer Evolution I-IX. Used an iron block and belt‑driven timing system, making it more robust for high‑boost applications but heavier and less refined than the 4B11T's aluminium block.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 4B11T - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 4B11T can be a viable option for owners of lower‑value Evo Xs, but the engine is often subjected to hard use and tuning. Only consider a used unit with documented proof of recent timing chain replacement, turbo health, and oil consumption history. Without that, factor in £1,500-£3,000 for preventative work (chain, rings, turbo). Link once: /services/used-engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper 4B11T recon is the gold standard for Evo X owners. A quality recon should include: full strip and inspection, new timing chain and tensioner (critical), new piston rings (to address oil consumption), turbocharger refurbishment, new gaskets and seals, and a full test. With a 12-24 month warranty, this gives you peace of mind that the engine's known weaknesses have been addressed - well worth the £3,500-£5,500 supply cost for a performance car. Link once: /services/reconditioned-engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified when the original engine has suffered catastrophic failure (chain jump, bearing failure, turbo disintegration) and the car is a cherished example or track‑day project. An upgraded rebuild should include forged pistons, upgraded rods, new bearings, a full cylinder head overhaul, and a upgraded oil pump. This is specialist territory and typically only makes sense for cars with strong residual value or competition use. Link once: /services/rebuilt-engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All engines can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted Mitsubishi Evo specialists nationwide, with 12‑month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units. Link once: /services/supply-and-fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The 4B11T sits in Lancer Evolution X - cars now worth £10,000-£35,000 depending on condition, mileage, and variant (especially FQ‑400). With a reconditioned supply cost of £3,500-£5,500, replacement is viable on most examples. However, for a high‑mileage standard GSR worth under £10,000, a used unit (£2,000-£3,500) with documented history may be the only sensible option. Given the Evo X's status as a modern classic, many owners choose to invest in a reconditioned engine to preserve the car's value and performance.

items.question: What are the most common failures on the 4B11T Evo X engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are timing chain stretch (causing rattling on start-up and potential chain jump), oil consumption (due to piston ring wear or PCV issues), and turbocharger failure (wastegate actuator, bearing wear). The engine is otherwise robust; regular servicing and using high-quality fully synthetic oil are essential for longevity. Timing chain: rattling on start-up is the early warning sign. Oil consumption: check oil levels regularly; piston ring replacement may be needed. Turbocharger: wastegate and bearing issues common on tuned engines.
bullets: Timing chain: rattling on start‑up is the early warning sign.
Oil consumption: check oil levels regularly; piston ring replacement may be needed.
Turbocharger: wastegate and bearing issues common on tuned engines.

items.question: Which Mitsubishi models use the 4B11T engine?
items.answer: The 4B11T was fitted exclusively to the Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution X (CZ4A chassis) from 2007 to 2015. UK variants include the 296 hp GSR/SST, 335 hp FQ-335, 359 hp FQ-360, and 403 hp FQ-400. US/export spec models produce 283 hp. Not to be confused with the 4B11 naturally aspirated engine. Not to be confused with the 4G63T from earlier Evos.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 4B11T engine?
items.answer: A used 4B11T can be viable for lower-value Evo Xs, but only if it has documented proof of recent timing chain replacement, turbo health, and oil consumption history. Without that, factor in £1,500-£3,000 for preventative work (chain, rings, turbo). A reconditioned engine is the safer choice - it includes new timing chain, piston rings, turbo refurbishment, and gaskets, with a 12-24 month warranty. Used is cheaper (£2,000-£3,500) but timing chain and oil consumption risks are significant. Reconditioned addresses all known weak points and gives peace of mind.
bullets: Used: cheaper (£2,000-£3,500) but timing chain and oil consumption risks are significant.
Reconditioned: addresses all known weak points and gives peace of mind.

items.question: How do I confirm if my car has the 4B11T or the 4B11?
items.answer: Check the engine code stamped on the block (left-hand side) - it will read 4B11T for the turbocharged Evo engine, or 4B11 for the naturally aspirated version. The V5C logbook also lists the full engine number, with the first 5 characters identifying the code. 4B11T: 2.0L turbo, 286-440 hp, Evo X only. 4B11: 2.0L naturally aspirated, 154 hp, used in Lancer, Outlander, ASX. Fitting the wrong variant is not a straight swap - different pistons, rods, ECU, turbo and ancillaries.

items.question: How long does a 4B11T engine typically last?
items.answer: With meticulous maintenance and early preventative work, these engines can exceed 100,000-150,000 miles. The 4B11T is fundamentally a robust engine; the limiting factors are the timing chain, oil consumption, and turbocharger wear. Timing chain replacement recommended at 60k-80k miles as preventative. Regular oil changes (5,000 miles) with high-quality fully synthetic 5W-30/5W-40 oil are essential. Oil level checks should be performed regularly between services.
